text:
nina_cs: Quick sync 11 onboarding with MeadowLabs hitting auth/rate ceiling during init. Their devs see immediate 200s then a burst of 429s right after the ephemeral token rotates. Theyre using browser-sdk v0.9.2 behind a company proxy. Any fast triage tips? :eyes:

leo_eng: This smells like a token-rotation stampede. How many parallel init calls? If they fan out to multiple endpoints on first load it's easy to blow the per-key window.

nina_cs: They reported opening 9 workers that each call embeddings+chat warmup. Log snippet they pasted: 
```
2026-04-04T11:22:10Z INFO token_refresh ok user=meadow id=mw-77 ttl=60s
2026-04-04T11:22:11Z WARN http retry status=429 x-request-id=r-9001 attempts=4
2026-04-04T11:22:12Z WARN http retry status=429 x-request-id=r-9002 attempts=2
```
Proxy sometimes rewrites keepalives per them.

anya_sdk: 9 parallel warmups = high. Two quick client tests: 1) set `maxParallelInit: 3` in SDK, 2) add a randomized splay on token refresh (200-600ms). If 429s drop, recommend client-side splay and backoff.

leo_eng: If they can't change prod fast, ops can do a one-off: bump ephemeral TTL for their API key from 60s -> 120s for 24h and enable soft-smoothing on the key. Pros: fewer rotations; cons: longer-lived tokens (documented). Need CS lead + ops sign-off.

nina_cs: I drafted a short playbook for ops and asked MeadowLabs for permission to apply the temporary platform tweak. Also asked them to capture `x-request-id` and `x-ratewindow` for ingress correlation.

ops-bot: Internal note created on case ML-2190 by nina_cs: "probable preflight stampede at token rotate; suggested client splay; offered TTL bump + soft-shed if client changes infeasible"

leo_eng: For the playbook diagnostics: grep ingress logs for the API key and check if burst originates from a single IP or multiple IPs. Commands: 
```
grep "x-request-id" /var/log/redwood/ingress.log | grep <api_key>
awk '/x-ratewindow/ {print $0}' /var/log/redwood/ingress.log | grep <api_key>
```
If bursts come from multiple IPs, it's multi-tab/workers client-side. If single IP, proxy replay likely.

anya_sdk: Also ask them to verify their proxy doesn't replay Authorization headers on retry or clone requests. Double headers can trick the limiter into counting separate identities.

nina_cs: MeadowLabs agreed to try the client repro in staging (splay + reduce parallel init) and gave permission to apply TTL bump if the repro fails. I scheduled the ops window for 02:00 UTC tomorrow if needed.

leo_eng: One more ops note: when we enable soft-smoothing, set an automated rollback at +24h and add alert that watches 429 rate and token reuse anomalies. Include steps to revert TTL and smoothing flags.

nina_cs: Great. I'll update the ticket ML-2190 with the playbook and the monitoring dashboard link. Thanks all. :pray:
